title: Sync the dispatch-guard area spec with the one-door refusal behavior
action: Merge the behavior delta of the capped behavior_change cells dod-1 and dod-4 into the area spec. The synthesis is already done — apply it as written, in the spec's own business vocabulary (no file, function, command, or crate names outside the Pointers section; the spec calls a herding slot a PANE WORKER and a cli slot an EXTERNAL COMMAND, keep that vocabulary). THREE EDITS. (1) In B16a, the bullet that begins `- What stays refused: a wholly bare dispatch, an unconfigured model name, an`: extend `any tier resolving to an external command` to `any tier resolving to an external command or a pane worker`. Then add one new bullet immediately after that bullet, titled in bold `Every refusal names the one verb that resolves the transport.` Its content: a tier backed by an external command or a pane worker is not a helper at all; the guard evaluates a helper dispatch and can only permit or refuse it, never turn it into the shell call such a tier actually needs; so each of those refusals hands back the single preparation verb that reads the configured slot and returns the tool plus the exact payload to run, and shows the hand-written shell shape only as an illustration of what that verb returns; an actor that reads nothing but the refusal recovers on its next attempt; and the bare refusal states the ACTUAL kind of the work tier's slot — pane worker, external command, or unconfigured — instead of a fixed phrase, because naming a pane-worker slot an external command sent readers to a remedy that could not work. (2) In B18, the sentence beginning `Drift between a rendered helper file's model and the configured slot is surfaced as an **advisory** by the status snapshot and the configuration check`: the advisory now covers ALL FOUR rendered identities. It previously checked only three — the execution tier's writing identity was rendered but never drift-checked, so a stale copy of it sat unreported beside a changed slot. Also state that the advisory names the slot's actual kind (pane worker, external command, or unconfigured) rather than one fixed phrase, and that its remedy names a command that runs in the repo the advisory is printed for: a project that is not itself a bee checkout cannot run the onboarding verb directly and is pointed at the installer instead. Keep the rest of that sentence — advisory never a refusal, the dispatch-time agreement rules already protect the dispatch — unchanged. (3) Frontmatter: append to `bee.decisions` an entry naming dispatch-one-door D1 (every helper dispatch resolves its transport from configuration through one preparation verb; refusals name that verb; a pane-worker slot is named honestly, 2026-08-21), and append to `bee.sources` an entry naming the dispatch-one-door cells dod-1 and dod-4 with the date 2026-08-21. Do not touch `timestamp`, `bee.id`, `bee.lifecycle`, `bee.areas`, `bee.required_context` or `bee.authoritative_for`. Do not restructure the document, do not renumber any behavior, and do not add a Pointers entry.
